title: Vertex lighting has edge flicker at resolutions lower than 324 pixels
body:
### Tested versions

Tested in 4.5.1*, 4.6dev1

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 22631) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8180) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 15.92 GiB memory

### Issue description

At resolutions lower than 324 pixels, vertex lighting seems to break in a way that suggests it's not accounting for vertices at the edge of the screen. If width is less than 324 pixels it occurs on the right edge of the screen, and if height is less than 324 it occurs on the bottom edge. If both are less than 324 it occurs both on the right and bottom edge. 

The light is not culled and there are no shadowcasters.

Demonstration (I also added the minimum project I used to isolate this with no custom models):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a06fc8a-2b9e-402d-9bf9-3f84b0e2f957

Note that project is at render scale 0.5 hence the resolution in settings is doubled.


Seems related to this closed issue https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/98440 (does not seem cover this lower resolution) but not related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/105063 as the light itself is not being culled.



### Steps to reproduce

- enable vertex light override in project settings
- set viewport resolution width or height to 323 or below (or reduce 3d render scale such that `viewport resolution * render scale < 324`)

The issue is easier to see when the camera is rotating.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[vertex-light-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23978868/vertex-light-test.zip)
